definition: Angles that fill the space all the way round one point; they add up to $360^{\circ}$, and angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$.
The pair of angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross; they are always equal.
The total of the interior angles of a shape: $180^{\circ}$ for a triangle, $360^{\circ}$ for a quadrilateral and $(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$ for a polygon with $n$ sides.
Two angles in the same position at the two places where a line crosses a pair of parallel lines; they are equal.
Two angles between a pair of parallel lines, on opposite sides of the line that crosses them, in a Z shape; they are equal.
Two angles between a pair of parallel lines, on the same side of the line that crosses them; they add up to $180^{\circ}$.
The angle inside a polygon at one of its vertices.
The angle between one side of a polygon and the next side extended past the vertex; at a vertex that is not reflex, the interior and exterior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
A polygon whose sides are all equal and whose angles are all equal.
